_comment: Hand labelled Arabic name pairs. same=true means both spellings refer to the same person and should normalize to the same string. same=false means they are genuinely different people and must NOT collapse together. The brief asks for 100 pairs and this is 36, chosen to cover each spelling phenomenon rather than to hit a number. Expanding it is real labelling work and the false pairs matter most because they are what catch over aggressive normalization.

pairs.why: hamza inside a name with article
final ya vs alef maksura with article
one letter apart but different people
country vs news network and only two letters apart
ta vs tah are genuinely different letters

_known_limitations_comment: Pairs that ARE the same name but that my normalization does not catch. I keep them here as xfail instead of deleting them or relabelling them false. Deleting would hide the gap and relabelling would be a lie about the language. If a future normalization change makes one of these pass the test suite tells me so and I move it up into pairs.

known_limitations.why: hamza on waw folds to waw but bare hamza is deleted so one keeps a letter the other loses. fixing it means dropping hamza seats entirely which breaks مسؤول vs مسئول instead
same word with the hamza on different seats. waw seat folds to waw and ya seat folds to ya so they never meet
